title: Spectroscopic monitoring of long secondary period variables. The case of J-type carbon stars
summary: Long-secondary-period (LSP) variables are a subclass of long-period variables whose origin is a matter of debate. J-type carbon stars are a subclass of carbon stars enriched in 13C, and the origin of this chemical peculiarity is unclear. In this paper, we report on the discovery of a LSP in two J-type carbon stars: VZ Per and UV Cam. Methods. A decade-long spectroscopic monitoring was used to obtain a long-term radial-velocity curve for the two stars. From a frequency analysis, we isolated a LSP signal. The retrieved periodicity was then compared with changes in spectral profiles and available light-curve variability to further constrain the origin of the modulation. Results. For VZ Per, the LSP derived from the radial-velocity curve (~960 days) is correlated with the light-curve dimming event and a variation in the Balmer absorption line profile. These results translate into changes in the gas and dust column densities with the phase of the LSP, with the maximum gas column density occurring ahead of the dust. For UV Cam, the radial velocity monitoring yields a period of ~1178 d with an amplitude of about 1 km/s. Interpreting the RV modulation as a Keplerian signal for both stars, a low-mass (<0.1Msun) close companion is found. In this scenario, variations in gas and dust column densities with (orbital) phase trace the material in the expanding comet-like tail trailing the substellar companion. Conclusions. These observations provide time-dependent variations of the gas and dust in LSP variables that are consistent with the current binary scenario. Furthermore, the detection of LSP among J-type carbon stars anchors their current evolutionary status in the dust-producing region of the thermally-pulsing AGB phase.

AI.tldr: Two J-type carbon stars (VZ Per, UV Cam) are newly identified as LSP variables; their radial-velocity periods and correlated gas/dust changes support a binary (substellar companion) scenario and place them in the dust-producing thermally-pulsing AGB phase.
AI.motivation: The origin of LSP variability is debated, and the 13C enrichment of J-type carbon stars is chemically unexplained; testing whether J-type carbon stars host LSPs can constrain both puzzles and clarify their evolutionary state.
AI.method: Decade-long spectroscopic monitoring produced long-term radial-velocity curves for VZ Per and UV Cam. Frequency analysis isolated the LSP signal; retrieved periodicities were compared with spectral-profile changes and available light-curve variability. RV modulation was interpreted as a Keplerian (binary) signal, and gas/dust column densities were traced with orbital phase.
AI.result: VZ Per: LSP of ~960 d, correlated with a light-curve dimming event and Balmer absorption-line profile variation, indicating gas and dust column-density changes with maximum gas ahead of dust. UV Cam: RV period ~1178 d with amplitude ~1 km/s. Keplerian interpretation implies a low-mass (<0.1 Msun) close companion for both; phase-dependent gas/dust variations trace material in an expanding comet-like tail behind the substellar companion.
AI.conclusion: The observed time-dependent gas and dust variations in these LSP variables are consistent with the current binary scenario. Detecting LSPs among J-type carbon stars anchors their evolutionary status in the dust-producing region of the thermally-pulsing AGB phase.

title: A forest of emission lines observed by Sunrise III/SUSI above the solar limb
summary: We present off-limb spectroscopy using low-straylight data from the Sunrise Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUSI) onboard the Sunrise III stratospheric solar observatory. A spatial scan with SUSI's slit almost parallel to the local limb reached from within the solar disc to 6.5 Mm off-limb. The wavelength range spanned from 407.6 to 410.25 nm. We detected a total of 174 spectral lines in emission off-limb, a 2.5-fold increase over previous reports. Surprisingly, 122 of these lines begin to appear in emission already on the disc, although close to the limb. In addition, one-fifth of relatively prominent emission lines are due to rare-earth and heavy elements and molecules, where the absorption lines of these transitions are typically weak on-disc.

AI.tldr: Off-limb spectroscopy with Sunrise III/SUSI (407.6–410.25 nm) reveals 174 emission lines off-limb, 2.5× more than previously reported, with 122 already appearing in emission near the limb and ~20% of prominent lines from rare-earth/heavy elements and molecules.
AI.motivation: Previous off-limb spectral line inventories were limited in number and sensitivity; low-straylight observations are needed to detect weak off-limb emission and clarify where lines transition into emission.
AI.method: Low-straylight SUSI spectroscopy onboard the Sunrise III stratospheric solar observatory, using a spatial scan with the slit nearly parallel to the local limb, extending from within the disc to 6.5 Mm off-limb, covering 407.6–410.25 nm.
AI.result: Detected 174 off-limb spectral emission lines, a 2.5-fold increase over prior reports. 122 of these lines begin in emission already on the disc near the limb. One-fifth of relatively prominent emission lines arise from rare-earth and heavy elements and molecules, whose absorption transitions are typically weak on-disc.
AI.conclusion: Low-straylight off-limb spectroscopy substantially expands the inventory of off-limb emission lines and shows that many form close to or on the disc and that rare-earth/heavy-element and molecular lines contribute notably to the prominent off-limb emission spectrum.

title: Stellar parameters and abundances for 3.2 million DESI DR1 spectra using machine learning
summary: We present a machine-learning pipeline for determining stellar parameters and chemical abundances from spectra observed by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Building on the model-driven Payne framework, we train an artificial neural network on ~370,000 synthetic spectra spanning FGK stars, and fit the network directly to the flux-calibrated, un-normalised spectral energy distribution (SED) of each star, rather than to a continuum-normalised spectrum as done by DESI's official Stellar Parameter (SP) pipeline. Internal accuracy tests show a median interpolation error of less than 0.3% for 90% of a synthetic verification sample, and the full fitting workflow recovers input labels to high accuracy even at low signal-to-noise ratio (S/N). Validating our method on cross-matched samples of 6719 APOGEE and 3455 GALAH stars observed by DESI with S/N > 20, we recover Teff and logg with smaller systematic offsets than the DESI SP pipeline, an improvement we attribute to fitting the full SED shape rather than a normalised spectrum. We further recover 12 elemental abundances (Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Ni, Ba, and Y) to an accuracy that matches or exceeds SP where a comparison is possible, and provide four abundances, Mn, V, Ba, and Y, that SP does not report at all. Applying this pipeline to the DESI Data Release 1 stellar sample, we deliver a catalogue of stellar parameters and abundances for 3.2 million stars.

AI.tldr: A machine-learning pipeline trained on ~370k synthetic FGK spectra fits the full flux-calibrated SED of DESI stars, outperforming DESI's official SP pipeline in Teff/logg accuracy and delivering 12 elemental abundances (including 4 not reported by SP) for 3.2 million stars in DR1.
AI.motivation: DESI's official Stellar Parameter pipeline fits a continuum-normalised spectrum, which discards the overall SED shape and can introduce systematic offsets in derived stellar parameters. The authors seek a more accurate approach for determining stellar parameters and chemical abundances from DESI spectra.
AI.method: Building on the model-driven Payne framework, an artificial neural network is trained on ~370,000 synthetic FGK spectra. Unlike the SP pipeline, the network is fitted directly to the flux-calibrated, un-normalised SED of each star rather than a continuum-normalised spectrum.
AI.result: Internal tests show <0.3% median interpolation error for 90% of a synthetic verification sample, with high accuracy even at low S/N. Validation on 6719 APOGEE and 3455 GALAH cross-matched stars (S/N > 20) yields smaller systematic Teff and logg offsets than SP, attributed to full-SED fitting. Twelve abundances (Na, Mg, Al, Si, Ca, Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Ni, Ba, Y) are recovered at accuracy matching or exceeding SP, plus four (Mn, V, Ba, Y) not reported by SP.
AI.conclusion: The full-SED machine-learning approach improves on DESI's SP pipeline and enables additional abundance determinations. Applied to DESI Data Release 1, the pipeline produces a catalogue of stellar parameters and abundances for 3.2 million stars.

title: Cross-Modal Solar Image Synthesis: Adapting the Surya Foundation Model from He I 10830 Å to EUV Translation and Coronal Hole Segmentation
summary: The long observational record of He I 10830 Å offers a means to investigate solar morphology before modern extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) imaging. We adapt the Surya solar foundation model to predict Solar Dynamics Observatory/Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (SDO/AIA) 94, 193, and 304 Å images and a coronal hole (CH) probability map from full-disk helium observations. A convolutional input adapter, low-rank backbone updates, and dedicated output decoders learn from temporally paired, geometrically registered observations, with Spatial Possibilistic Clustering Algorithm (SPOCA) catalog polygons providing CH supervision. On observations held out from downstream fine-tuning, the selected dedicated models achieve disk-restricted correlation coefficients (CCs) of 0.8196, 0.8885, and 0.8398 for the three AIA channels, respectively; the CH model achieves an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.4360. The predictions recover broad solar structure, although local agreement varies substantially by channel. An optional residual refiner addresses spatial detail, and its application on pre-SDO dates improves the correlation of synthetic AIA 304 with Solar and Heliospheric Observatory/Extreme-ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SOHO/EIT) 304 references from 0.6511 to 0.7085. Together, these results support the feasibility of helium-conditioned EUV morphological proxies and motivate their use in historical reconstruction, within the scope of the downstream test and cross-instrument evaluation.

AI.tldr: The authors adapt the Surya solar foundation model to map full-disk He I 10830 Å observations to SDO/AIA 94, 193, 304 Å images and a coronal hole probability map, achieving moderate-to-strong correlations and feasible historical EUV proxies.
AI.motivation: The extended historical record of He I 10830 Å observations enables investigation of solar morphology prior to the modern EUV imaging era, but a means to translate helium observations into EUV-like morphological proxies is lacking.
AI.method: They adapt the Surya solar foundation model using a convolutional input adapter, low-rank backbone updates, and dedicated output decoders, trained on temporally paired, geometrically registered observations, with SPOCA catalog polygons supervising coronal hole prediction. An optional residual refiner is used to improve spatial detail.
AI.result: On held-out observations, disk-restricted correlation coefficients reach 0.8196, 0.8885, and 0.8398 for AIA 94, 193, and 304 Å; the coronal hole model attains an IoU of 0.4360. Applying the residual refiner to pre-SDO dates improves synthetic AIA 304 vs. SOHO/EIT 304 correlation from 0.6511 to 0.7085.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate the feasibility of helium-conditioned EUV morphological proxies and motivate their use for historical solar reconstruction, within the scope of downstream testing and cross-instrument evaluation.

title: SWAN-SF-V2: A Multivariate Time Series Dataset for Space Weather Data Analytics; Now with AIA and Weighted SHARP Parameters
summary: Since its original publication in 2020, the SWAN-SF dataset has been cited in over 300 research publications. Here we describe a comprehensive update to the original multivariate time series (MVTS) dataset extracted from solar photospheric vector magnetograms in the Spaceweather HMI Active Region Patch (SHARP) series. As was performed in the original release, our dataset includes a cross-checked NOAA solar flare catalog that facilitates the comparative evaluation of methods designed for solar flare prediction. We discuss the methods used for data collection, cleaning, and pre-processing of the solar active region and flare data, which includes improvements to the data integration and sampling methodology. Additional parameters have been derived from the Solar Dynamics Observatory's Atmospheric Imaging Assembly to augment the original features derived from magnetogram data. Our dataset expands the period of observations to cover 7,730 MVTS data collections from active regions occurring between May 2010 and December 2025, each of which is composed of 182 flare-predictive parameters. We continue to integrate flare reports, with over 39,000 multi-source verified flare reports providing flaring history information about the source active regions. The primary tasks enabled by the disseminated dataset continue to include optimization of solar flare prediction and detailed investigation for elusive flare predictors or precursors, with both operational (research-to-operations), and basic research (operations-to-research) benefits.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a comprehensive update to the SWAN-SF multivariate time series dataset for solar flare prediction, expanding to 7,730 active region samples (May 2010–December 2025) with 182 flare-predictive parameters and over 39,000 verified flare reports.
AI.motivation: The original SWAN-SF dataset (2020) has been widely cited (300+ publications), motivating an updated, improved version. The update aims to support solar flare prediction optimization and investigation of elusive flare predictors/precursors, with both operational and basic research benefits.
AI.method: The authors describe improved methods for data collection, cleaning, and pre-processing of solar active region and flare data, including enhancements to data integration and sampling methodology. They derive additional parameters from SDO's Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) to augment the original magnetogram-derived features, and integrate a cross-checked, multi-source NOAA solar flare catalog with over 39,000 verified flare reports.
AI.result: The dataset expands to 7,730 MVTS data collections from active regions between May 2010 and December 2025, each composed of 182 flare-predictive parameters. The flare catalog provides flaring history information about source active regions via 39,000+ multi-source verified reports.
AI.conclusion: The upgraded SWAN-SF dataset remains a resource for optimizing solar flare prediction and investigating flare predictors/precursors, benefiting both research-to-operations and operations-to-research efforts.

title: Global solar compressible convection simulations on non-Cartesian mappings
comment: Accepted to A&A. 14 Pages + Appendix. 20 Figures + 5 Appendix Figures
summary: Context. Modeling the global dynamics of the Sun requires numerical frameworks capable of simulating the highly turbulent convective envelope and its coupling with the stable radiative interior. Simulating such spherical domains in standard cartesian finite-volume codes presents significant topological challenges. Aims. The goal is to extend the cartesian Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) framework Dyablo to non-cartesian geometries in order to perform global solar convection simulations that extend all the way down to the stellar core. Methods. We introduced a mapped grid approach within the Dyablo framework to build Dyablo Whole Sun (DWS) code. We implemented an $α-β$ well-balanced scheme to preserve hydrostatic equilibrium. Furthermore, we present a robust methodology to generate fully integrated solar background profiles from $r=0$ to the surface. Results. We validated the implementation using standard hydrodynamic tests and ran high-resolution 2D global solar convection simulations on a disk grid. Conclusions. Our models successfully capture the turbulent convective broad slow upflows and narrow fast downflows and the excitation of acoustic waves and p modes. The interaction of strong downflowing plumes with the top of the radiative zone, successfully excites internal gravity waves in the radiative interior.

AI.tldr: The authors extend the Cartesian AMR code Dyablo to non-Cartesian (mapped) geometry, creating the DWS code, which performs 2D global solar convection simulations reaching the stellar core with a well-balanced scheme and full solar background profiles.
AI.motivation: Simulating global solar dynamics requires modeling the turbulent convective envelope coupled to the stable radiative interior, but spherical domains are topologically difficult in standard Cartesian finite-volume AMR codes.
AI.method: They introduce a mapped-grid approach in Dyablo (DWS), implement an alpha-beta well-balanced scheme to preserve hydrostatic equilibrium, and develop a methodology to build fully integrated solar background profiles from r=0 to the surface.
AI.result: The implementation is validated with standard hydrodynamic tests, and high-resolution 2D global solar convection simulations are run on a disk grid.
AI.conclusion: The models reproduce turbulent convection with broad slow upflows and narrow fast downflows, excite acoustic waves and p modes, and show that strong downflowing plumes hitting the radiative-zone top excite internal gravity waves in the radiative interior.

title: Measured energy exchange in coronal hole solar wind from its solar origins to the heliosphere
comment: The manuscript has been accepted to ApJ
summary: Coordinated ground- and space-based remote observations are used to provide a comprehensive, multi-perspective view of the solar atmosphere that we connect with in situ measurements in the heliosphere centered around the April 8 2024 Total Solar Eclipse observed across North America. These near-contemporaneous, multi-wavelength datasets are used to directly derive the plasma parameters and compute an energy budget of a solar wind stream at its low-coronal birthplace (at an altitude of 1.05Rsun). The energy budget is also independently computed at and beyond the Alfvén surface from the in situ observations of the same stream. The total wave energy flux dominates the low-coronal budget (11 W m-2 Alfvén, 7 to 23 W m-2 in compressive MHD modes), while enthalpy (13 W m-2) and work done against gravity from 1.0Rsun (2.5 W m-2) make up the remainder. The total coronal energy budget is consistent with the total measured in situ by Parker Solar Probe if and only if compressive energy flux is included and attributed to the fast magnetosonic mode. Nearly all this thermal and wave energy is converted to ion heating, acceleration and gravitational potential energy within the Alfvén surface. The stream evolution is well-described as a thermal-pressure driven wind with additional energy deposited by MHD fluctuations. The observed evolution of the Alfvénic component of these fluctuations follows a near-dissipation-free curve below the Alfvén surface while deviating from it more strongly above this critical surface.

AI.tldr: Multi-wavelength ground- and space-based observations around the April 8, 2024 total solar eclipse, combined with Parker Solar Probe in situ data, are used to derive plasma parameters and close the energy budget of a solar wind stream from its low-coronal birthplace (1.05 Rsun) through the Alfvén surface, showing that wave energy dominates and that ion heating, acceleration, and gravitational potential energy account for nearly all thermal and wave energy below the Alfvén surface.
AI.motivation: Understanding how the solar wind is energized requires connecting its source region in the low corona to its in situ state in the heliosphere. The April 8, 2024 total solar eclipse across North America provided a rare opportunity to obtain coordinated, multi-perspective remote observations of the solar atmosphere that could be linked to near-contemporaneous in situ measurements of the same solar wind stream.
AI.method: Coordinated ground- and space-based, multi-wavelength remote observations around the April 8, 2024 eclipse were combined with in situ heliospheric measurements to derive plasma parameters and compute an energy budget of a solar wind stream at its low-coronal birthplace (1.05 Rsun). An independent energy budget was also computed at and beyond the Alfvén surface from in situ observations of the same stream, with the compressive energy flux attributed to the fast magnetosonic mode.
AI.result: At 1.05 Rsun, the total wave energy flux dominates the low-coronal budget (11 W m-2 Alfvénic, 7-23 W m-2 in compressive MHD modes), while enthalpy (13 W m-2) and work done against gravity from 1.0 Rsun (2.5 W m-2) make up the remainder. The coronal energy budget matches the total measured in situ by Parker Solar Probe only if the compressive energy flux is included and attributed to the fast magnetosonic mode. Nearly all thermal and wave energy is converted to ion heating, acceleration, and gravitational potential energy within the Alfvén surface. The Alfvénic component follows a near-dissipation-free curve below the Alfvén surface but deviates more strongly above this critical surface.
AI.conclusion: The solar wind stream evolution is well described as a thermal-pressure driven wind with additional energy deposited by MHD fluctuations. Closing the energy budget across the Alfvén surface requires including the compressive (fast magnetosonic) energy flux, and the observed evolution of the Alfvénic fluctuations indicates near-dissipation-free propagation below the Alfvén surface with enhanced deviation above it.

title: SPHERE/ZIMPOL observations of the symbiotic system R Aquarii. II. Dynamics of the dust in the Mira wind and the Halpha gas in the jet
comment: 25 pages, 22 figures, accepted by Astonomy & Astrophysics
summary: R Aqr is a resolved symbiotic Mira binary and a prototype target for the study of complex hydrodynamic processes including dust-driven mass loss, mass transfer, accretion, and jet outflows and the formation of strongly asymmetric structures. We investigate for R Aqr the central Halpha emission from the ionized gas and the polarization from scattering dust based on SPHERE/ZIMPOL maps with a resolution of about 25 mas (5 AU). Data for four epochs were taken, including the dust eclipse around 2021, to follow structural changes. The central Halpha gas traces the orbital motion of the hot component. The polarization from scattering dust shows interaction effects near the binary (<60 AU), including a flattened distribution in the orbital plane, corotating dust, and a reduction of the scattering signal during the dust eclipse. The polarization shows at >60 AU a steady outflow with about a dozen dust clouds, a few of which have a comet-like core and tail features. The dust velocity is about 20 km/s, and this is faster than for the CO gas measured with ALMA. Several prominent Halpha clouds also show scattering polarization because they are just partly ionized dust clouds from the Mira wind. We also found small faster-moving transient Halpha clouds, pointing to outflow instabilities and shocks. The observed angular shift of Halpha during the dust eclipse, can be explained by strong illumination changes from the hot component. At larger separation, the H$α$ clouds move faster (>100 km/s), in agreement with previous studies. This acceleration is probably a result of gas heating by photoionization and shocks, and the produced overpressure gives rise to the two well-known jet-like features expanding in polar directions. The presented R Aqr data are very useful to clarify the complex hydrodynamics taking place in AGB binaries.

AI.tldr: High-resolution SPHERE/ZIMPOL maps of the symbiotic Mira binary R Aqr reveal Halpha gas tracing orbital motion and scattering polarization from dust showing near-binary interaction, corotating dust, dust eclipse effects, and a steady outflow with comet-like dust clouds and jet-related acceleration.
AI.motivation: R Aqr serves as a prototype symbiotic Mira binary for studying complex hydrodynamics such as dust-driven mass loss, mass transfer, accretion, jet outflows, and asymmetric structure formation; the work aims to resolve the central gas and dust behavior and its structural evolution.
AI.method: SPHERE/ZIMPOL polarimetric and Halpha imaging at about 25 mas (5 AU) resolution over four epochs, including the 2021 dust eclipse, isolating central Halpha emission from ionized gas and polarization from scattering dust.
AI.result: Central Halpha traces the hot component's orbital motion; scattering polarization reveals flattened orbital-plane dust, corotating dust, and reduced scattering during the dust eclipse within <60 AU. Beyond 60 AU, a steady outflow with about a dozen dust clouds (some comet-like with cores and tails) moves at about 20 km/s, faster than ALMA CO gas. Several prominent Halpha clouds show scattering polarization as partly ionized Mira-wind dust. Small faster-moving transient Halpha clouds indicate outflow instabilities and shocks. The Halpha angular shift during the dust eclipse is explained by strong illumination changes, and outer Halpha clouds move faster (>100 km/s), consistent with prior work.
AI.conclusion: Acceleration of Halpha clouds is likely driven by gas heating from photoionization and shocks, with resulting overpressure producing the two known jet-like polar features; the R Aqr dataset helps clarify the complex hydrodynamics of AGB binaries.

title: AI Agents as a Research Team: A Human-Supervised Case Study in Stellar Spectroscopy
comment: 32 pages and 11 figures. This paper showcases the power of agentic workflow in the development of research projects
summary: We present a qualitative case study of a human-supervised team of specialized AI agents supporting an astronomy research project. The Bot Spectroscopist team, described in the project record as operating through Grok Bot powered by xAI Grok, divided work among orchestration, numerical implementation, data curation, spectroscopy critique, literature search, figure preparation, manuscript editing, and review. Human decisions determined scientific scope, model changes, and manuscript inclusion. The scientific application is CondGen, a deterministic label-to-spectrum network extending our previous work to five individual elemental abundances. The reported baseline assessment achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.003681 in continuum-normalized flux on 21,657 synthetic test spectra. Existing binned diagnostics show that reconstruction error varies with effective temperature and abundance. The bots also flagged a non-monotonic cool-star magnesium response for further investigation; a matched SYNSPEC abundance sweep is needed to assess its physical fidelity. Building on a pre-existing spectral database, notebooks, and research program, the authors estimate that the reported analysis, diagnostics, figure preparation, and initial manuscript drafting were assembled in less than a week through human prompting and exchanges among agents. No comparison with a human team starting from the same resources was performed, so this elapsed-time account does not establish a productivity or labor saving. The study illustrates task delegation, artifact exchange, critique, and correction under human supervision.

title: ZTF J191814.28+010850.2: An eclipsing cataclysmic-variable candidate in the SW Sextantis period range
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures. Published in BAV Journal No. 114 (2026)
summary: We present a photometric study of ZTF J191814.28+010850.2, a short-period variable previously classified as an EA-type eclipsing binary. The analysis is based on ZTF observations in the g and r bands and additional time-series CCD photometry obtained on two nights. We derive an eclipse period of 0.1408529(3) d. The phased ZTF light curves show a deep primary eclipse, with an eclipse depth of about 2.8 mag in g and 2.0 mag in r, as well as indications of cycle-to-cycle variations outside eclipse. After excluding the primary eclipse and accounting for the remaining orbital modulation, robust locally weighted fits reveal a broad non-linear long-term brightness variation in both bands, with peak-to-peak ranges of about 0.56 mag in g and 0.46 mag in r. The deep eclipse, short orbital period and irregular variability suggest that the object is a cataclysmic-variable candidate and possibly a member of the SW Sextantis group. Time-resolved spectroscopy is required to confirm or refute the proposed classification and to test possible membership in the SW Sex class.

AI.tldr: Photometric study of ZTF J191814.28+010850.2, formerly an EA-type eclipsing binary, reveals a 0.1408529 d period with deep eclipses and long-term variability, suggesting a cataclysmic variable, possibly SW Sextantis.
AI.motivation: The object was previously classified as an EA-type eclipsing binary, but a deep eclipse combined with a short orbital period and irregular out-of-eclipse variability is inconsistent with a normal eclipsing binary, motivating a re-examination of its nature.
AI.method: Analysis of ZTF g- and r-band observations plus two nights of time-series CCD photometry; derivation of the eclipse period; phased light-curve construction; removal of the primary eclipse and orbital modulation; robust locally weighted (lowess) fitting to isolate long-term brightness variations; comparison of eclipse depth and variability with cataclysmic-variable characteristics.
AI.result: Eclipse period of 0.1408529(3) d. Primary eclipse depth of ~2.8 mag in g and ~2.0 mag in r, with cycle-to-cycle variations outside eclipse. A broad non-linear long-term brightness variation appears in both bands, with peak-to-peak amplitudes of ~0.56 mag in g and ~0.46 mag in r.
AI.conclusion: The deep eclipse, short orbital period, and irregular variability indicate the object is a cataclysmic-variable candidate, possibly belonging to the SW Sextantis group. Time-resolved spectroscopy is needed to confirm or refute this classification and test SW Sex membership.

title: Fast and Differentiable MHD Surrogate for Solar Wind using Neural Operator
summary: Global magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations provide the complete plasma state of the heliosphere, but their computational cost limits applications requiring repeated model evaluations. We introduce SNOW (Solar Neural Operator for Wind), a fast and differentiable surrogate for global MHD solar wind. SNOW combines a rotational ballistic approximation, a spherical harmonic neural operator, and causal radial context to autoregressively propagate all eight MHD variables from 20 to 240 Rs through consecutive shell to shell transitions. Trained and evaluated using AWSoM simulations spanning a solar cycle, SNOW remains stable across the complete rollout. The model successfully reproduces the large scale plasma and magnetic field structures, including fast and slow wind streams, magnetic polarity sectors, vector orientations, fieldline connectivity, and bulk-flow structures. Additionally, the magnetic divergence and induction diagnostics remain comparable to the reference MHD solutions. The complete three-dimensional solution is generated in less than one second on a single GPU. These results demonstrate the feasibility of fast neural emulation of global MHD solar wind solutions while retaining physically meaningful plasma and magnetic field structure.

AI.tldr: SNOW, a fast differentiable neural surrogate for global MHD solar wind, autoregressively propagates all eight MHD variables from 20 to 240 Rs in under one second per 3D solution on a single GPU while retaining physically meaningful plasma and magnetic field structure.
AI.motivation: Global MHD simulations give a complete plasma state of the heliosphere but are computationally expensive, limiting applications that need repeated model evaluations. A fast, differentiable surrogate is needed to enable such repeated evaluations without sacrificing physical fidelity.
AI.method: SNOW combines a rotational ballistic approximation, a spherical harmonic neural operator, and causal radial context. It autoregressively propagates all eight MHD variables from 20 to 240 Rs via consecutive shell-to-shell transitions, and is trained and evaluated on AWSoM simulations spanning a solar cycle.
AI.result: The model remains stable across the complete rollout and reproduces large-scale plasma and magnetic field structures, including fast and slow wind streams, magnetic polarity sectors, vector orientations, fieldline connectivity, and bulk-flow structures. Magnetic divergence and induction diagnostics remain comparable to reference MHD solutions. The full 3D solution is generated in under one second on a single GPU.
AI.conclusion: These results demonstrate the feasibility of fast neural emulation of global MHD solar wind solutions while retaining physically meaningful plasma and magnetic field structure.

title: Unravelling the Nature of AT\,2025abao: From Precursor to Final Fate
comment: Accepted by ApJL, comments are very welcome. softwares and data are listed by the urls below https://github.com/czlovemath123/guangqi1d https://raw.githubusercontent.com/czlovemath123/guangqi1d/master/modules/lrne/wfst.dat 10.5281/zenodo.23149482
summary: Luminous red novae (LRNe) are potential signatures of common envelope evolution (CEE), a critical yet poorly understood phase in compact binary formation. AT\,2025abao, an LRN in the Andromeda galaxy, originated from an asymptotic giant branch (AGB) progenitor and exhibited a prolonged pre-outburst transient. Lacking direct constraints on the companion, however, the system's evolutionary fate remains unclear. Here, we unravel the binary nature of AT\,2025abao by modeling its complete evolution, from precursor to final outcome. We show that the eight-year infrared precursor arises from a $\approx1.4^{+0.2}_{-0.3}\,M_{\odot}$ main-sequence companion inspiralling through the wind of a $\approx 6.9\,M_{\odot}$ AGB star. As CEE commences, the companion plunges into the envelope and launches a shock. Radiation hydrodynamic modeling of this outburst constrains the total ejecta mass to $\approx 0.92\,M_{\odot}$ and energy to $\approx 1.25\times 10^{47}\,$erg, revealing that only $\approx 0.57\,M_{\odot}$ becomes unbound. Subsequent radiative transfer simulations successfully reproduce the evolving spectral energy distribution. Crucially, our models indicate the main-sequence companion and AGB core survive in an eccentric orbit without merging at least 400 days after CEE onset. AT\,2025abao may therefore be the first observed CEE event caught forming a close compact binary, bridging a long-standing observational gap in compact binary formation.

AI.tldr: Modeling of LRN AT 2025abao reveals a ~1.4 M_sun main-sequence companion inspiraling into a ~6.9 M_sun AGB star, producing a shock-driven outburst with ~0.92 M_sun ejecta; both stars survive in an eccentric orbit, marking a CEE event caught forming a compact binary.
AI.motivation: Luminous red novae are potential signatures of common envelope evolution (CEE), a critical but poorly understood phase in compact binary formation. AT 2025abao, an LRN in Andromeda from an AGB progenitor with a prolonged pre-outburst transient, lacked direct constraints on its companion, leaving its evolutionary fate unclear.
AI.method: The authors model the complete evolution of AT 2025abao from precursor to final outcome, combining an inspiral model of a main-sequence companion through the AGB wind, radiation hydrodynamic modeling of the CEE-onset outburst, and subsequent radiative transfer simulations of the spectral energy distribution.
AI.result: The eight-year infrared precursor is attributed to a ~1.4 (+0.2/-0.3) M_sun main-sequence companion inspiraling through the wind of a ~6.9 M_sun AGB star. The outburst modeling constrains total ejecta mass to ~0.92 M_sun and energy to ~1.25e47 erg, with only ~0.57 M_sun becoming unbound. Radiative transfer simulations reproduce the evolving SED. The companion and AGB core survive in an eccentric orbit without merging at least 400 days after CEE onset.
AI.conclusion: AT 2025abao may be the first observed CEE event caught in the act of forming a close compact binary, bridging a long-standing observational gap in compact binary formation.

title: From the Milky Way to the Early Universe: How Metallicity Shapes the Formation of Double Neutron Stars
comment: 27 pages, 14 figures, submitted to AAS Journals. Comments are welcome
summary: Among the compact binaries detected through gravitational wave (GW) emission, double neutron stars (DNSs) hold the unique distinction of having well-characterized local analogs in the Milky Way. However, understanding their broader cosmological population remains challenging due to the complex metallicity-dependent evolution of their progenitors. Using the detailed binary population synthesis code POSYDON, we model DNS formation across a cosmological range of metallicities. We find that while DNSs are predominantly formed through common envelope evolution, metallicity-dependent radial expansion and stellar wind mass loss bifurcates the pathway into distinct subchannels, producing systematically distinct merging populations at different metallicities. Notably, our best representative Galactic models predict local merger rates in broad agreement with the latest GWTC-5 constraints, suggesting that the populations observed via radio pulsar surveys and through GW emission need not be in tension. Contrary to previous studies, we demonstrate that the intrinsic merger efficiency increases toward low metallicities, a trend robust across varying binary evolution assumptions, although the magnitude and the underlying stellar processes driving this enhancement vary across metallicity regimes. When convolved with the cosmic star formation history, our models reveal that the majority of merging DNSs originate from progenitors in the range $\sim 0.1\,Z_\odot - Z_\odot$, with significant supersolar contributions. Furthermore, we show that weaker stellar winds at low metallicities produce DNS mergers with systematically more symmetric mass ratios ($q \gtrsim0.9$). Additionally, we assess detectability within proposed configurations for third-generation GW observatories. Our study provides a framework for interpreting the cosmological DNS population in the upcoming multi-messenger era.

AI.tldr: Using POSYDON binary population synthesis, the authors model double neutron star (DNS) formation across a cosmological metallicity range, showing that metallicity-dependent evolution bifurcates the common-envelope pathway, raises intrinsic merger efficiency toward low metallicity, and yields systematically more symmetric mass ratios, with local rates consistent with GWTC-5.
AI.motivation: DNSs are the only compact binaries with well-characterized Milky Way analogs, yet their broader cosmological population is poorly constrained because progenitor evolution depends strongly and complexly on metallicity. Resolving whether radio-pulsar and GW-observed populations are in tension, and characterizing metallicity trends, requires dedicated population synthesis over a cosmological metallicity range.
AI.method: The detailed binary population synthesis code POSYDON is used to model DNS formation across a cosmological range of metallicities, tracking metallicity-dependent radial expansion, stellar wind mass loss, and common envelope evolution. The resulting populations are convolved with the cosmic star formation history, compared with GWTC-5 local merger-rate constraints, and assessed for detectability with proposed third-generation GW observatories.
AI.result: DNSs form predominantly via common envelope evolution, but metallicity-dependent radial expansion and wind mass loss bifurcate this into distinct subchannels, producing systematically distinct merging populations at different metallicities. Best representative Galactic models predict local merger rates broadly consistent with GWTC-5, implying radio pulsar and GW populations need not be in tension. Intrinsic merger efficiency increases toward low metallicity, robust across binary evolution assumptions though its magnitude and driving stellar processes vary by metallicity regime. Convolved with cosmic star formation history, most merging DNSs originate from progenitors at ~0.1-1 Z_sun, with significant supersolar contributions. Weaker winds at low metallicity yield more symmetric mass ratios (q ≳ 0.9). Detectability within proposed third-generation GW observatory configurations is also assessed.
AI.conclusion: Metallicity is a primary driver shaping the cosmological DNS merger population, bifurcating formation channels, enhancing merger efficiency at low metallicity, and producing more symmetric mass ratios, while reconciling local radio and GW rate estimates. The framework supports interpreting the cosmological DNS population in the upcoming multi-messenger era.

title: Coherent radio bursts, polarity reversal, and quiescent emission from the M4V dwarf WW PsA
comment: 14 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, accepted for publication in PASA
summary: Coherent radio emission from magnetically active M dwarfs is largely observed in two varieties: stochastic solar-like bursts and beamed, rotationally modulated emission including auroral pulses. Detailed monitoring of these stars is critical for probing the plasmas and magnetic fields driving the emission. We conducted a search for polarised radio emission from stars within 85 pc, covering $2.2\times10^4$ h of stellar dynamic spectra from the ASKAP Deep Investigation of Neutral Gas Origins (DINGO) survey. We report the discovery of coherent radio bursts from the M4V dwarf WW PsA. In addition to quiescent emission, we detect three long-duration ($\gtrsim$30 min) bursts, each ~100% circularly polarised, in 283.3 h of data. We also report a fourth burst in an epoch not covered by our search, detected using the VASTER pipeline. One of the bursts features a polarity reversal midway through, based on which we favour the electron cyclotron maser (ECM) mechanism over plasma emission. We tentatively propose the bursts are due to rotationally modulated ECM pulses of variable intensity. We infer the required physical properties of WW PsA, including a high obliquity $β= 74^{+6}_{-22}$ deg under an oblique rotator model.

AI.tldr: The ASKAP DINGO survey search for polarised radio emission within 85 pc uncovered coherent radio bursts from the M4V dwarf WW PsA, including three ~100% circularly polarised, long-duration bursts, one showing a polarity reversal consistent with the electron cyclotron maser mechanism.
AI.motivation: Coherent radio emission from magnetically active M dwarfs appears mainly as stochastic solar-like bursts or beamed, rotationally modulated emission such as auroral pulses. Long-term monitoring is essential to probe the plasmas and magnetic fields powering this emission, motivating a systematic polarised radio search over a large volume.
AI.method: A search for polarised radio emission from stars within 85 pc using $2.2\times10^4$ h of stellar dynamic spectra from the ASKAP DINGO survey, supplemented by a VASTER pipeline detection. Physical properties of WW PsA were inferred by fitting an oblique rotator model to the burst emission.
AI.result: Coherent radio bursts were discovered from the M4V dwarf WW PsA. Besides quiescent emission, three long-duration ($\gtrsim$30 min) bursts, each ~100% circularly polarised, were detected in 283.3 h of data, plus a fourth burst in an epoch outside the search coverage (VASTER). One burst shows a polarity reversal midway through, favouring the electron cyclotron maser mechanism over plasma emission. A high obliquity of $β=74^{+6}_{-22}$ deg is inferred.
AI.conclusion: The bursts are tentatively attributed to rotationally modulated ECM pulses of variable intensity. The polarity reversal supports the ECM mechanism, and the oblique rotator fit yields a high obliquity for WW PsA, demonstrating the value of wide-field polarised surveys for characterising M dwarf magnetospheres.

title: Magnetohydrodynamic coronal modelling with high-fidelity magnetograms
summary: To resolve coronal structures in detail, it is essential to constrain the coronal model using high-fidelity magnetograms with minimal smoothing. In this paper, we improve the numerical stability of COCONUT to enable efficient coronal MHD simulations driven directly by photospheric magnetograms, including magnetic field strengths exceeding 1000 Gauss (G), and then use it to investigate the impact of small-scale magnetic field structures that are typically filtered out of photospheric magnetograms on the coronal simulation results. We constrain this model with two types of magnetograms: the high-fidelity HMI photospheric magnetogram with only minor preprocessing through Gaussian smoothing, which preserves magnetic field strengths reaching 1500 G, and one processed using 50th-order filtered spherical harmonics, where the magnetic field strength is limited to below 100 G. The results demonstrate that the COCONUT can reproduce the large-scale coronal structures revealed by pB and EUV observations. Compared with the coronal MHD simulation constrained by a conventionally filtered magnetogram, the simulation constrained by the high-fidelity magnetogram yields approximately $50\%$ more OMF and produces EUV images that are more consistent with the observations. Moreover, the results show that when viewed from low latitudes in certain EUV passbands, such as the 193~Å channel, open-field regions near the solar poles may appear as bright structures that are typically associated with closed-field regions. This finding highlights the need for solar polar-orbiting missions to overcome the limitations and ambiguities arising from the restricted view of the polar regions from the ecliptic plane and to provide more complete full-Sun observations.

AI.tldr: This paper enhances the numerical stability of the COCONUT coronal MHD model to allow simulations driven directly by high-fidelity photospheric magnetograms (fields >1000 G), showing that preserving small-scale magnetic structures increases open magnetic flux by ~50% and improves EUV image agreement with observations.
AI.motivation: Resolving coronal structures in detail requires constraining coronal models with high-fidelity magnetograms that undergo minimal smoothing. Conventional magnetograms filter out small-scale magnetic structures, potentially degrading simulation fidelity and biasing derived quantities such as open magnetic flux (OMF) and EUV morphology.
AI.method: The numerical stability of COCONUT is improved to enable efficient coronal MHD simulations driven directly by photospheric magnetograms with field strengths exceeding 1000 G. Two magnetogram types are compared: (1) a high-fidelity HMI magnetogram with only minor Gaussian smoothing, preserving fields up to 1500 G; and (2) a magnetogram processed with 50th-order filtered spherical harmonics, limiting field strength below 100 G.
AI.result: COCONUT reproduces large-scale coronal structures revealed by pB and EUV observations. The high-fidelity magnetogram simulation yields ~50% more OMF and produces EUV images more consistent with observations than the conventionally filtered case. Additionally, in certain low-latitude viewing geometries and EUV passbands (e.g., 193 Å), open-field regions near the solar poles may appear as bright structures typically associated with closed-field regions.
AI.conclusion: Preserving small-scale magnetic structures in magnetograms is crucial for accurate coronal MHD simulations, significantly affecting OMF and EUV morphology. The viewing-angle dependence of polar open-field appearance underscores the need for solar polar-orbiting missions to overcome limitations and ambiguities from the ecliptic-plane view and provide complete full-Sun observations.

title: Detection of knots in the supernova type Iax remnant Pa 30
comment: 15 pages, 10 figures. In press at ApJ
summary: We present deep, narrowband Gemini North/GMOS images of the Pa 30 nebula that reveal rich small-scale structure in the ejecta filaments. In [S II], the number of detected filaments increases by about an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. The imaging further reveals that the filaments are not smooth radial streaks, but instead are composed of cascades of knots or clumps. The images in [O III] yield the first confirmation that previously detected diffuse [O III] emission in fact originates from the same [S II] filaments. We measure a nebula center consistent with the position of the central star, indicating that the remnant has not received a large transverse kick. The 3$σ$ upper limit on the velocity of the stellar kick is $\lesssim$100 km/s. Cross-sectional profiles of the filaments in [S II] and [O III] show a central peak on top of a nebular background, the latter being likely due to diffuse emission or unresolved filaments. The median [S II] width of 0.7'' is slightly broader than the 0.50'' seeing, providing some evidence of partially resolved filaments and implying a characteristic knot diameter of ${\sim}10^{16}$ cm. The $\approx$1'' widths measured in [O III] are consistent with the poorer seeing of the oxygen images. The discovery of this clumpy substructure provides a new observational constraint on models for the origin and evolution of the remarkable filamentary ejecta of Pa 30.

AI.tldr: Deep GMOS narrowband imaging of Pa 30 reveals an order-of-magnitude more ejecta filaments than previously known, showing they are clumpy knot cascades rather than smooth streaks, with a nebula center coincident with the central star and a tight upper limit on any stellar transverse kick.
AI.motivation: Previous studies of the Pa 30 nebula lacked the depth and spatial resolution to characterize its ejecta filaments in detail, leaving open questions about filament morphology, the origin of diffuse [O III] emission, and whether the remnant has experienced a significant transverse kick.
AI.method: Deep, narrowband Gemini North/GMOS imaging of Pa 30 in [S II] and [O III], including filament detection and counting, comparison with previous studies, determination of the nebula center relative to the central star, velocity upper limits from the kick, and cross-sectional profile analysis of filament widths against seeing.
AI.result: The number of detected [S II] filaments increases by about an order of magnitude. Filaments are not smooth radial streaks but cascades of knots/clumps. [O III] emission is confirmed to originate from the same [S II] filaments. The nebula center agrees with the central star position, with a 3σ upper limit on stellar kick velocity of ≲100 km/s. Filament profiles show a central peak atop a nebular background; median [S II] width is 0.7'' (slightly broader than 0.50'' seeing), implying a characteristic knot diameter of ~10^16 cm, while ~1'' [O III] widths are consistent with poorer seeing.
AI.conclusion: The newly discovered clumpy substructure of Pa 30's filaments provides a fresh observational constraint on models for the origin and evolution of its remarkable filamentary ejecta, and the lack of a large transverse kick supports a symmetric or low-kick formation scenario.

title: Three-dimensional magnetic reconnection in unipolar regions. A case study of coronal bright points in the Sun
summary: Magnetic reconnection is a fundamental mechanism underlying the heating and a wide variety of eruptive phenomena in the solar atmosphere; however, characterizing its 3D aspects remains challenging. Our aim is to understand how 3D magnetic reconnection in unipolar regions drives localized heating and plasma ejections. To this end, we used a self-consistent 3D radiation-MHD simulation of a coronal bright point (CBP) performed with the Bifrost code. We focused on localized, intense heating events and upflows near a unipolar CBP footpoint associated with its parasitic polarity. 3D reconnection diagnostics were carried out using the parallel electric field and its integral along magnetic field lines. We then compared the resulting upflows with spectroscopic observations from Hinode/EIS. We find recurrent episodes of 3D magnetic reconnection without nulls at the footpoints of loops rooted near the CBP's parasitic polarity. A detailed analysis of one representative event places the reconnection region at heights z=[1.0,2.5] Mm, within a predominantly vertical magnetic field with localized concentrations of electric current. The dissipation of these currents efficiently heats the plasma to about 2 MK and produces strong gas-pressure gradients that drive upflows of a few tens of km/s. Blueshifts observed with Hinode/EIS near the parasitic polarity of an observed CBP are consistent with this scenario. The recurrence of these reconnection events are essential for heating CBP loops to million-degree temperatures. This form of 3D reconnection may operate more generally in the solar atmosphere, dissipating magnetic stress around strong flux concentrations and contributing to heating in apparently unipolar regions. The resulting pressure-driven upflows offer an indirect spectroscopic diagnostic of localized reconnection heating, which future observations with MUSE and Solar-C will be able to test.

AI.tldr: Using a self-consistent 3D radiation-MHD simulation (Bifrost) of a coronal bright point, the authors identify recurrent 3D magnetic reconnection events without magnetic nulls that locally heat plasma to ~2 MK and drive pressure-driven upflows, consistent with Hinode/EIS blueshifts.
AI.motivation: Magnetic reconnection fundamentally drives heating and eruptive phenomena in the solar atmosphere, yet characterizing its 3D aspects remains challenging. The authors aim to understand how 3D reconnection in unipolar regions produces localized heating and plasma ejections, specifically near a coronal bright point (CBP) footpoint associated with its parasitic polarity.
AI.method: A self-consistent 3D radiation-MHD simulation of a CBP was run with the Bifrost code. The study focused on localized, intense heating events and upflows near a unipolar CBP footpoint linked to its parasitic polarity. 3D reconnection diagnostics used the parallel electric field and its integral along magnetic field lines. Resulting upflows were compared with Hinode/EIS spectroscopic observations.
AI.result: Recurrent 3D reconnection episodes without nulls occur at loop footpoints rooted near the CBP's parasitic polarity. One representative event places the reconnection region at z=[1.0,2.5] Mm in a predominantly vertical field with localized current concentrations. Current dissipation heats plasma to ~2 MK, generating strong gas-pressure gradients that drive upflows of a few tens of km/s. Hinode/EIS blueshifts near the parasitic polarity of an observed CBP match this scenario.
AI.conclusion: Recurrent 3D reconnection without nulls is essential for heating CBP loops to million-degree temperatures. This form of reconnection may operate generally in the solar atmosphere, dissipating magnetic stress around strong flux concentrations and heating apparently unipolar regions. Pressure-driven upflows provide an indirect spectroscopic diagnostic of localized reconnection heating, testable with future MUSE and Solar-C observations.

title: Ap stars with resolved magnetically split lines: Mean magnetic field modulus measurements 1999--2004
comment: 20 pages, 40 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Magnetic Ap stars that have a strong enough field and a sufficiently low v sin i show spectral lines resolved into their magnetically split components. This allows their mean magnetic field modulus <B> to be determined. We complement the existing knowledge of the rotational magnetic variability and of the binarity of a sample of 34 Ap stars with resolved magnetically split lines by analysing observations obtained between 1999 and 2004 that had not been exploited before and, when available, observatory archive data. We determine the values of <B> and of the radial velocity by measuring the magnetic splitting and the wavelength shift of the Fe lambda 6149.2 Å line in high-resolution spectra recorded in natural light. Combining our measurements with published ones, we characterise the variability of both quantities. We derived for the first time the accurate, unambiguous values of the rotation periods of HD 29578 and HD 165474. We set lower limits of years to decades to the rotation periods of six stars and identified four more that have not shown any significant <B> variations over timescales of 13 to 33 years. We established that HD 47103 is the first Ap star with a rotation period of years known to have a magnetic field significantly exceeding 7.5 kG. We achieved the first determination of the orbital elements of HD 116114, HD 142070, and HD 144897, and we refined the orbital elements of six other binaries.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 1999–2004 and archival spectra of 34 magnetic Ap stars with resolved magnetically split lines yields new rotation periods, period lower limits, long-term <B> stability findings, and orbital elements for several binaries.
AI.motivation: Ap stars with strong fields and low v sin i exhibit magnetically split spectral lines, enabling determination of the mean magnetic field modulus <B>. Existing knowledge of rotational magnetic variability and binarity for a sample of 34 such stars was incomplete, and previously unanalyzed observations could refine it.
AI.method: High-resolution spectra recorded in natural light, obtained between 1999 and 2004 (previously unexploited) plus observatory archive data, were analyzed. <B> and radial velocity were derived from the magnetic splitting and wavelength shift of the Fe λ 6149.2 Å line. Combined with published measurements, the variability of both quantities was characterized.
AI.result: Accurate, unambiguous rotation periods were derived for the first time for HD 29578 and HD 165474. Lower limits of years to decades were set on the rotation periods of six stars, and four more stars showed no significant <B> variations over 13–33 years. HD 47103 was identified as the first Ap star with a rotation period of years known to have a field significantly exceeding 7.5 kG. Orbital elements were determined for the first time for HD 116114, HD 142070, and HD 144897, and refined for six other binaries.
AI.conclusion: The study expands the rotational and binary characterization of 34 Ap stars with resolved magnetically split lines, providing new periods and period limits, evidence of long-term <B> stability, and new or refined orbital elements, thereby improving constraints on the magnetic and dynamical properties of these stars.

title: Production of White Dwarf Debris Disks from Planetary Collisions and Poynting-Robertson Drag
comment: 44 pages, 7 figures, accepted for publication in PASP
summary: This paper explores the production of debris disks around white dwarfs, which are observed to experience frequent pollution events. In this scenario, planetary collisions occur just outside the surface of a highly evolved AGB star, after the end of its mass loss phase, as it starts its transition into a white dwarf. The collisions vaporize a fraction of the planetary material, which subsequently expands, cools, nucleates droplets, and condenses into rocky bodies with characteristic size of order $s\sim1$ cm. The rocky debris disk evolves through the action of Poynting-Robertson drag, driven by the stellar luminosity, which is initially large but steadily decreases with time. This scenario provides an alternate channel for delivering rocky material to the immediate vicinity of a white dwarf.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes that planetary collisions just outside a highly evolved AGB star can vaporize planetary material, which recondenses into ~1 cm rocky bodies and forms a debris disk around the emerging white dwarf, offering an alternative route for delivering rocky material close to the white dwarf.
AI.motivation: White dwarfs are observed to experience frequent pollution events, indicating that rocky material is delivered to their immediate vicinity. A mechanism is needed to explain how this rocky debris is produced and transported near the white dwarf.
AI.method: The scenario posits planetary collisions occurring just outside the surface of a highly evolved AGB star after the end of its mass-loss phase, during its transition to a white dwarf. The collisions vaporize a fraction of the planetary material, which expands, cools, nucleates droplets, and condenses into rocky bodies with characteristic size s ~ 1 cm. The resulting rocky debris disk is then evolved through Poynting-Robertson drag driven by the stellar luminosity, which is initially large but decreases steadily with time.
AI.result: The collisions produce vaporized planetary material that recondenses into rocky bodies of order ~1 cm in size, forming a debris disk whose evolution is governed by Poynting-Robertson drag under a declining stellar luminosity.
AI.conclusion: This scenario provides an alternate channel for delivering rocky material to the immediate vicinity of a white dwarf.
